body.statement:
Assume the following two statistical premises.  First, for every \(0<a<b<\infty\),
\[
\sup_{\substack{\ell\in\mathcal M_n\\a\leq \ell/\sqrt n\leq b}}
\left|n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(\ell)-\Phi(\ell/\sqrt n)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{I}
\]
Second, sequential endpoint coercivity holds: for every sequence \(\ell_n\in\mathcal M_n\),
\[
\frac{\ell_n}{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow0
\quad\hbox{or}\quad
\frac{\ell_n}{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow\infty
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(\ell_n)\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{II}
\]
Then \(e_n=\inf_{\ell\in\mathcal M_n}\mathcal E_n(\ell)\) is positive for all sufficiently large \(n\), and every \(m_n\in\mathcal M_n\) satisfying \(\mathcal E_n(m_n)/e_n\to1\) obeys
\[
\frac{m_n}{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow t^{\star},
\qquad
n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m_n)\longrightarrow C^{\star}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
C^{\star}=\min_{t>0}\Phi(t)
=\max_{(a,b)\in\operatorname{conv}\{(A(\beta),B(\beta)):\beta\in\mathcal K\}}
2\sqrt{ab}>0,
\]
the minimizer \(t^{\star}\) is unique, and an optimizing convex combination is supported on at most two parameter values active at \(t^{\star}\).  This is a conditional argmin-transfer theorem; it does not assert premises \((\mathrm I)\) and \((\mathrm{II})\) from the current statistical assumptions.
body.justification: The theorem gives a complete and auditable deterministic transfer from statistical uniform convergence and endpoint coercivity to a unique balanced pilot scale.
body.gap: Yamin provides the analogous optimization architecture for a different binary-arm rate, while the statistical premises for this factorial square-root envelope remain open.
body.consumer: Stable-batch factorial replications may use the two-state certificate only after separately verifying the stated compact-window and endpoint premises.
body.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}deterministic\text{-}envelope\text{-}certificate}\), \(\Phi\) has the unique minimizer \(t^{\star}>0\), its minimum is \(C^{\star}>0\), and the convex-hull formula and two-active-point certificate in the statement hold.  It remains to transfer this deterministic conclusion to the balanced discrete problems.

Because \(Q\mid n\), every multiple of \(Q\) has a balanced complement.  Choose \(\widetilde m_n\in\mathcal M_n\) to be a nearest admissible multiple of \(Q\) to \(t^{\star}\sqrt n\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), this point is between \(Q\) and \(n-Q\), and
\[
\left|\frac{\widetilde m_n}{\sqrt n}-t^{\star}\right|
\leq\frac Q{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{19}
\]
Choose \(0<a<t^{\star}<b<\infty\).  Premise \((\mathrm I)\), continuity of \(\Phi\), and (19) give
\[
n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(\widetilde m_n)\longrightarrow
\Phi(t^{\star})=C^{\star}.
\tag{20}
\]
Thus, with \(e_n=\min_{\ell\in\mathcal M_n}\mathcal E_n(\ell)\) (the minimum exists because \(\mathcal M_n\) is finite),
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}n^{3/2}e_n\leq C^{\star}.
\tag{21}
\]

Let \(\ell_n\) be an exact minimizer.  By (20), \(n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(\ell_n)\leq C^{\star}+1\) eventually.  Premise \((\mathrm{II})\) forces the ratios \(\ell_n/\sqrt n\) to remain bounded away from both zero and infinity.  Indeed, failure of either bound would produce a subsequence converging to the corresponding endpoint and contradict \((\mathrm{II})\).  Every subsequence therefore has a further subsequence on which
\[
\frac{\ell_n}{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow t_0\in(0,\infty).
\]
On a compact interval containing that subsequence, premise \((\mathrm I)\) yields
\[
n^{3/2}e_n-\Phi(\ell_n/\sqrt n)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{22}
\]
Equations (21)--(22) imply \(\Phi(t_0)\leq C^{\star}\).  Minimality of \(C^{\star}\) gives equality, and uniqueness gives \(t_0=t^{\star}\).  Since every convergent subsequence has this limit,
\[
\frac{\ell_n}{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow t^{\star},
\qquad n^{3/2}e_n\longrightarrow C^{\star}.
\tag{23}
\]
Because \(C^{\star}>0\), (23) also proves \(e_n>0\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).

Now let \(m_n\) satisfy \(\mathcal E_n(m_n)/e_n\to1\).  From (23),
\[
n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m_n)
=\frac{\mathcal E_n(m_n)}{e_n}\,n^{3/2}e_n
\longrightarrow C^{\star}.
\tag{24}
\]
Premise \((\mathrm{II})\) again confines \(m_n/\sqrt n\) to a compact subinterval of \((0,\infty)\).  Along any convergent subsequence with limit \(t_1\), premise \((\mathrm I)\) and (24) give \(\Phi(t_1)=C^{\star}\).  Uniqueness forces \(t_1=t^{\star}\), proving convergence of the full sequence and completing the implication.
